newFindings.whatHappened: All 14 failures are in scenario A of lifecycle-durability. The root one is the driver: `waited 120000ms for the long-running bash call; saw lifecycle, task_kind, error, error, error, error, turn_complete, lifecycle, lifecycle`. The run under test had already ENDED — four consecutive errors exhausted its retries and the turn completed — but the driver has no way to learn that, so it waited its full 120 s deadline and the 13 assertions that read the run's artifacts then failed in 0.0x ms each.
twoSeparableProblems: The engine's loopback fetch to its own mock failed four times in a row under whole-directory load. Not reproduced a second time, so it is a flake and its cause is unestablished; the mock server and the engine were in the same process tree either way.

The rig turns one flake into 120 s and 14 red tests. `Run.waitForEvent` rejects only on its own deadline; a waiter that also rejected when the child exits or emits turn_complete would fail in seconds and name the real reason.

behaviorChanges.change: macOS plugin hosts are now REFUSED. A plugin whose manifest declares a non-loopback host no longer starts on macOS unless [extensions] allowUnsandboxedTools names it — the refusal Linux has always given. Loopback endpoints are unaffected. This can break a working macOS setup on upgrade; the failure is loud and names the flag.
behaviorChanges.cost: It broke the SHIPPED example plugin, which declares example.com:443, and the only gate that runs that example as shipped went red. Fixed in 33cea48 by grading the example against the rule it now meets, and by asserting that the refusal reaches drainMcpNotices.

behaviorChanges.change: Every install now prints what ~/.rune/bin holds (files, generations, MB) and, above five generations, what pruning would reclaim. Nothing is deleted without --prune-backups / RUNE_PRUNE_BACKUPS=1.

The reaper is gated on identity. A leftover row is only signalled when the live process at that pid carries the recorded kernel start time. Rows written by an older rune-tools, or on a machine whose identity cannot be read, are FORGOTTEN instead of killed — so a mixed-version ~/.rune/bin reaps less, never wrong. Windows is unchanged.

A command mismatch is treated as an exec, not a stranger: /bin/sh -c "sleep 90" execs into sleep within ~30 ms with an unchanged start time, so `command` is recorded and reported but never gates the kill.
A child that leaves its process group (setsid) is documented as out of scope on macOS/noop, in active_child.rs and docs/sandbox.md. Linux is covered by bwrap's PID namespace.
registerDelegationTools now THROWS if the store is missing rather than degrading in silence. A constructor reordering cannot be caught by tsc; only the loud failure can.
CheckRecord and Evidence gained an optional `digest`; Evidence gained `staleAt`. Old rows have neither and are treated as before.
The lifecycle projection's `revision` now reports the tree as of the moment the event is emitted (memoised 1 s), not the run's opening snapshot. At most two short git calls per second of run.
A model-run check that executed NO test no longer closes a step. It is still counted as executed, still on the check ledger, still cited — the new CheckRelation reason is "no_tests".
Relatedness reads an inline script's body through stripLiterals, keeping only module-load arguments (require/import/open/readFile/from). A path in a comment or a log string no longer buys scope.
The retro's filesWritten counter now includes worker-authored files, so its numbers rise for runs that delegated.

Worker id scheme is now w<12 hex>-<n>, the hex being a sha256 digest of the WHOLE session id (was: the first 8 characters). Ids from before this change do not collide with ids after it. ids.json is read under an exclusive lock, written tmp+rename, and its 32-session prune keeps the session being allocated for.

A lease row now carries hostId and the holder's process start time. A local pid probe judges only a LOCAL lease; a foreign lease is bounded by TTL alone; where the OS will not say when a pid started, the lease is HONOURED (refusing a live holder is recoverable, stealing its task is not). The refusal text names the holder, where it is, how much is left (`expires in N minutes` — remaining, not maximum) and how it clears.

Crossing the 2 MiB per-run boundary budget emits exactly one delegation_notice (reason: boundary_budget, carrying lastCheckpointAt) and stamps the final checkpoint with boundaryBudgetExhausted. The budget now counts the whole serialized row, not just its messages.

The boundary-checkpoint dedup hashes the UNTRUNCATED transcript. Truncation notes and image placeholders each carry an 8-character digest of the bytes they replaced, so equal placeholders no longer imply equal content.

The worker reaper enumerates ignored files and commits them to the retained branch; over 16 MiB the checkout is KEPT with a reason naming the ignored output; node_modules and .venv are never carried onto a branch.
The durability suite's zero-spend claim is impossibility in three layers, not a row count of the founder's live database. That database is still read read-only and still printed, as a diagnostic.
tests/integration/plugin-examples.test.ts expects the two file tools, not http_get, and asserts the refusal reaches drainMcpNotices naming the tool and the flag.
